kernel.governing_law: The source's comparisons flow one direction only: beast-traits are measured against human/martial standards as the norm, and each ὡς clause subordinates creaturely feature to anthropic reference-class.
kernel.mutated_relation: The direction of the ὡς comparisons reverses: human and martial forms are the likenesses measured against creaturely originals, not the other way around.

clause_map.note: Death-flight reversal: creature-ground withdrawing from over-determined flesh, not death fleeing humans.
Locust is primary; horse, crown, human-face are derivative overlays — simile direction inverted.
Mammal-hair and leonine teeth are originals; gendered/human comparisons are the copies.
Chitin-carapace and wing-stridulation precede iron-plate and chariot-thunder — tools copied creature.

independent.recovered_law: In Text A the locusts (ἀκρίδες) are the described subject whose appearance is likened to horses and humans, while in Text B the roles are inverted: humans (ἄνθρωποι) are the described subject whose appearance is likened to locusts, and the horses are the ones who seek and cannot find (replacing the humans of 9:6). The direction of the simile-hierarchy and the identity of the seeking/suffering agent are thus reversed.
independent.law_match_note: Both describe the same reversal of simile direction—creatures vs. humans as the base/target of comparison—though the recovered claim adds detail about the seeking agent.
independent.terminal_note: The final portion of Text B (9:8–9) continues the inverted structure — humans bear animal likenesses (horse-hair, boar-teeth, tortoise-breastplates) and the sound is of locust-feet — so the reversed relation holds throughout.
